Topics · One God, one message

Isn't organised religion just about control?

Part of this is true, and the Quran says so. It describes a controlling guide and gives tests for anyone.

Part 1 of 4

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ ٱلْأَحْبَارِ وَٱلرُّهْبَانِ لَيَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَٰلَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْبَـٰطِلِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ ٱلذَّهَبَ وَٱلْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, indeed many of the scholars and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly[469] and avert [them] from the way of Allāh. And those who hoard gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allāh - give them tidings of a painful punishment.

Translator's notes

[469] i.e., through false pretense.

Quran · At-Tawbah 9:34

Start with the strong version, because it is partly true. Some who held religious authority have gathered wealth, used fear, and kept people from asking questions, and sometimes they were sincere. An honest account begins by saying so. What is striking is that the verse agrees. It speaks of many of the learned and the monks taking people's money wrongly and turning people from the way to God. And it is addressed to those who believe, as a caution to them.

A question for you

What have you seen up close?

If you sayMoney doing the talking
ThenThen you know why the verse is blunt about it. Wealth held at other people's expense is the first thing it names.
If you sayFear doing the talking
ThenFear has often been used to keep questions from being asked. The verse does not name fear, but the effect it does name, people being turned away from the path, fits.
If you sayPressure to belong or stay silent
ThenThat is real, and among the most common. The next verse is about what happens when a person's word outranks what you can check yourself.
If you sayMostly kindness, honestly
ThenThen you know both are possible, and that the question is what tells them apart. The parts ahead offer some tests.

Part 2 of 4

﴿ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَـٰنَهُمْ أَرْبَابًا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَسِيحَ ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓا۟ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَـٰهًا وَٰحِدًا ۖ لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ سُبْحَـٰنَهُۥ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allāh,[467] and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary.[468] And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.

Translator's notes

[467] By their obedience to them rather than to what Allāh ordained. [468] By their worship of him in conjunction with Allāh.

Quran · At-Tawbah 9:31

Translation

The Lord said, “Because this people draws near with their mouth and honors me with their lips, but they have removed their heart far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment of men which has been taught;

Original · Hebrew

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י יַ֚עַן כִּ֤י נִגַּשׁ֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה בְּפִ֤יו וּבִשְׂפָתָיו֙ כִּבְּד֔וּנִי וְלִבּ֖וֹ רִחַ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נִּי וַתְּהִ֤י יִרְאָתָם֙ אֹתִ֔י מִצְוַ֥ת אֲנָשִׁ֖ים מְלֻמָּדָֽה׃

Isaiah · 29:13

World English Bible

The second claim is subtler: they took their scholars and monks as lords besides God. The verse does not say how. Commentators explain it through obedience. When a person's word can overrule what the text itself says, and nobody may question, a teacher has become a ruler, whatever the title. The test is not whether you have teachers; you do. It is whether anyone's word outranks the source you could check.

A question for you

Where does a teacher become a ruler?

If you sayWhen I cannot question
ThenA fair line. Teaching that survives questions is stronger for them.
If you sayWhen disagreeing costs me
ThenThat is what turns advice into control. A price for dissent is among the clearest signs.
If you sayWhen what they say outranks the text
ThenThat is close to the verse's own picture: a human word placed above the one they were passing on.
If you sayWhen they profit from my agreement
ThenA practical test, and the last part comes back to it.

Part 3 of 4

﴿فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُذَكِّرٌ٢١ لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُصَيْطِرٍ٢٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

So remind, [O Muḥammad]; you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller.

Quran · Al-Ghashiyah 88:21-22

You yourself must make an effort. The Tathagatas (Buddhas) are only preachers. The thoughtful who enter the way are freed from the bondage of Mara.

Buddhist texts · Dhp 276

Max Müller, 1881

﴿لَآ إِكْرَاهَ فِى ٱلدِّينِ ۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَىِّ ۚ فَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِٱلطَّـٰغُوتِ وَيُؤْمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱسْتَمْسَكَ بِٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَا ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

There shall be no compulsion in [acceptance of] the religion. The right course has become distinct from the wrong. So whoever disbelieves in ṭāghūt[104] and believes in Allāh has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And Allāh is Hearing and Knowing.

Translator's notes

[104] False objects of worship, such as idols, heavenly bodies, spirits, human beings, etc.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:256

Translation

But I was willing to do nothing without your consent, that your goodness would not be as of necessity, but of free will.

Original · Ancient Greek

χωρὶς δὲ τῆς σῆς γνώμης οὐδὲν ἠθέλησα ποιῆσαι, ἵνα μὴ ὡς κατὰ ἀνάγκην τὸ ἀγαθόν σου ᾖ ἀλλὰ κατὰ ἑκούσιον·

Philemon · 1:14

World English Bible

Now the other half: what does the book say a messenger is? Not an enforcer. The verse tells him he is a reminder, and not set over people as a controller. Another verse, which you may know, says there is no compulsion in religion. If the person at the head of the chain is told he has no power to compel belief, then anyone below him who compels it acts against the source they cite.

A question for you

What would 'no compulsion' have to include to be real?

If you sayThat I can leave
ThenThat is the hardest one to honour, and the one that shows whether the rest is real.
If you sayThat I can disagree
ThenA community that cannot bear dissent leaves no room for these verses.
If you sayThat I can ask anything
ThenThe book itself records objections and answers them in many places. Questions are part of its own method.
If you sayAll of these
ThenThat is a high bar, and it is the bar these verses set. Communities of every kind, including those that read this book, have sometimes fallen short of it, and the verses remain the measure.

Part 4 of 4

﴿أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُ ۖ فَبِهُدَىٰهُمُ ٱقْتَدِهْ ۗ قُل لَّآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا ۖ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَـٰلَمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Those are the ones whom Allāh has guided, so from their guidance take an example. Say, "I ask of you for it [i.e., this message] no payment. It is not but a reminder for the worlds."

Quran · Al-An'am 6:90

A practical test follows. The guides the book holds up say: I ask you for no payment for this. A message given for nothing is hard to turn into a business. That does not mean no one may be paid for work; it means the message itself is not for sale. And the test can be turned on anyone: what do they gain if you agree? What does it cost them if you leave?

A question for you

Which question would you put to any guide before trusting them?

If you sayWhat do you gain if I agree?
ThenA fair question and an old one. The guides the book holds up answer it in the same words: nothing.
If you sayWhat happens if I leave?
ThenPerhaps the clearest of all. If leaving costs only the person's sadness, the relationship is probably honest.
If you sayCan I check what you say for myself?
ThenThat is the invitation the book makes for itself, as another question in this series shows.
If you sayDo you do what you ask of me?
ThenThe book asks this too, in another place, of those who say what they do not do.

The same in the other books

Translation

Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ἀναστήσονται ἄνδρες λαλοῦντες διεστραμμένα τοῦ ἀποσπᾶν τοὺς μαθητὰς ὀπίσω ἑαυτῶν·

Acts · 20:30

World English Bible

Translation

shepherd the flock of God which is among you, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion, but voluntarily; not for dishonest gain, but willingly;

Original · Ancient Greek

ποιμάνατε τὸ ἐν ὑμῖν ποίμνιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐπισκοποῦντες μὴ ἀναγκαστῶς ἀλλὰ ἑκουσίως κατὰ θεόν, μηδὲ αἰσχροκερδῶς ἀλλὰ προθύμως,

1 Peter · 5:2

World English Bible

Your reflection

Think of one community that has helped you without trying to own you. What did it do differently?
